svg.title: RMR control panel frame and deck plates
svg.text: RMR control panel: frame and deck plates
2020 frame 457 x 342.9 x 279.4 mm (inside 18 x 13.5 x 11 in) in two modules, on two 1/16 in 5052 deck plates, with 1/8 in acrylic walls. Views 1:5, detail E 2:1, printed at 100 %. Millimetres.
seen from above, front on the left; the DXF (y up) shows it from below
dashed: posts and bottom ring on the plate
4 x Ø5.5: M5 into the lower posts, with the feet
16 x Ø4.5: M4 x 6 into the bottom ring T-nuts, from below
Ø5.5 at (330, 150): PE stud, first screw of the lower ground bar
Drill through the acrylic template (sheet B's DXF plus this PE stud).
DIN rail and duct holes from the final layout: M4 x 12, nyloc nut below; the tails end 2.5 mm or more over the floor with the plate's sag (NutFits)
Ground bar screws, both plates: M5, plain nut below, tooth washer under the bar; the bar's foot + 8.5 to + 13.1 long (OpenScrews)
seen from above, front on the left; the DXF (y up) shows it from below
dashed: upper posts on the plate, mid ring under it
4 x Ø5.5: the locating studs. 16 x Ø4.5: M4 x 6 into the mid ring T-nuts
8 slots 4.5 wide, 25 to 39 from the edges: upper-post bracket screws, M4 x 10. PE stud at (425, 280)
Template: cut this DXF from 1/8 in acrylic; drill, then nibble the slots to it.
DIN rail and duct holes from the final layout: M4 x 12, nyloc below, 15 mm or more from each end
of the run; the tails end 13.1 mm or more over what stands below (HangGaps)
Shield clamp: M4 into a nyloc, the clamp's base + 8 to + 61.6 long; ground bar screws off the mid ring and its corner brackets (OpenScrews)
1: driver 24 V feeds, 0V-P returns. 2: SSR feeds and returns, servo 6 V. 3: X2, the E-stop latch, pin 43 sense. None over the 110 VAC compartment (y 183.9 up).
C Frame from the right side
mid ring 457: the upper module's platform
lid ring 457: off alone with 4 screws
base plate; feet add their height
E Plate on a ring rail
Euro 2020, 6 mm slot. Depth 6, lip 1.8, bore 4.2:
Base plate: the same joint upside down, from below.
Like a platform-framed house. Lower module:
base plate, bottom ring, 4 lower posts. Upper
module, built and wired on the bench: mid ring
standing on the plate, lid ring. It drops onto
4 M5 studs (50 long) in the lower post tops;
each passes the mid ring and the plate into a
Ø5.5 socket in its upper post, so the decks
line up within about 0.3 mm. 8 brackets from
the lower posts to the mid ring hold it down.
Corner brackets on the kit's M5 screws and
sliding T-nuts, slid in before a joint closes:
8 on the bottom ring, 8 lower posts to mid ring,
4 in the mid ring, 8 upper posts (rail legs on
the plate), 4 in the lid ring. Each plate,
screwed every 97 mm or less, keeps its ring
Each stops 0.5 short of the slot floor and
catches 3 or more threads of its spring T-nut:
back panel + washer: M5 x 8, tip 5.4
mount, front panel: M5 x 12, tip 5.3
mount, back panel: M5 x 10, tip 4.9
Lid M5 x 35 needs 15 of end tap; feet M5 x 16.
Anodize insulates: each rail is its own part.
Drill Ø4.2 through a slot floor into the bore,
tap M5; M5 x 16 with a ring lug and a tooth
washer. One 12 AWG home run per part to its
module's bar: lower 17 parts, 2 bars; upper 26, 2 bars.
DIN rails through their PE terminals, TB6600s
under an ear screw. Measure each part to PE
5 kg on a plate, simply supported on its ring
Cut list: 2020, 6 mm slot, from 1000 mm sticks
tap M5 top; drill Ø5.5 x 19 bottom
5424 mm in 20 pieces from 6 sticks (kerf 3, one squaring cut each):
Cut equal parts against one stop: the plates set the squareness.
Acrylic panels on 3 sheets of 24 x 18 in, each inside the 813 x 457 laser bed: one DXF per sheet, panels_acrylic_1.dxf
to _3.dxf. The aluminum lower back panel carries the inlet and the door cable's M20 gland (every mains part sits on
metal); drill and nibble it through panel_lower_back_template.dxf, cut from the spare sheet. Each part is drawn from
outside: u along x (front at 0) or y (left at 0), v up; turn it over to match. Screws Ø5.5 on the slot centre lines,
10 from each post end, ring screws at an even pitch, except the lower front and back panels: their bottom post screws
sit at 30 in vertical slots, through the gantry mount brackets, and they have no ring screw (sheet 5); the top has 8
into the lid ring and Ø10 over each lid screw. Vents: 21 slots 4 x 88 on 8 over the TB6600s. Cable entries: 5 desk
grommets in Ø50 holes (two upper left, upper front, upper right, lower left), each held by a Ø64 acrylic ring pressed
onto its sleeve behind the wall; caliper one grommet before cutting. Q0 is the inlet's switch if that is 2-pole. Read
back from the DXFs: least web 4 mm (2 needed). Order list: bom_frame.csv. NOT CUT YET, placeholders until the owner's
data: the PSU fan vent (its diameter), the IEC inlet with switch cut-out. Hold the lower side, right (acrylic 3) and
the back panel template until then.
the lower grommet's ring sets the lower posts (86). Measure
the first stick and a bracket leg, then rerun
Cut the list, equal parts against one stop.
Tap and drill the ends; drill and tap one
Lower module: feet and lower posts on the
base plate, bottom ring on brackets, plate
screws from below, studs in with threadlocker,
ground bar on the PE stud.
Build the lower deck, every 110 VAC terminal
Upper module, on the bench: mid ring on its
corner brackets, upper plate on it, upper
posts over the stud holes (a loose stud as a
pin) with their brackets, then the lid ring.
Ground bars on the upper PE stud; wire it.
Set it on the studs; 8 brackets to the lower
posts; plug the inter-deck terminals; clamp
the PE link; measure; panels last.
Two modules. Design, not yet built.
DXFs: both deck plates, panel sheets, template.
